# The dock shape gate fails open on a malformed zones container, not only its descriptors

## Context

Sibling of #18004, found while reviewing its fix (PR #18005). #18004 closed the **descriptor** arm of `Document.computeShapeFingerprint()`'s `edge-zone` walk: a present zone key whose descriptor cannot resolve to a node id now pushes an error instead of collapsing into the absent case. That fix is correct and I am not asking for it to be widened.

The identical fail-open survives **one level up**, at the `zones` container itself, and it is untouched by that fix. #18004's ACs are scoped to descriptor forms, so this is genuinely a separate input class rather than an incomplete fix.

Live latest-open sweep at 2026-09-01T03:45Z: read the latest 20 open issues, plus targeted searches over `computeShapeFingerprint`, `edge-zone container`, and `fingerprint zones container fail open` across open and closed. No equivalent exists. Nearest neighbour is #18004 itself (the descriptor arm) and #18000 (a failure *reporting* shape, not a gate).

## The Problem

`TopologyDiff.diffDockDocuments()` documents a fail-closed contract at `src/dashboard/dock/model/TopologyDiff.mjs:93`:

> a malformed or cyclic document yields `{…empty categories, errors: […]}` — no partial categories, no throw

When an `edge-zone` node's `zones` is present but is **not a JSON record**, the gate accepts it silently. Reproduced by execution against `origin/dev@68efc42bb2` via `npm run test-unit`:

```
zones = "main-split"  -> validate: 1 error | gate.errors: 0, shape "e{}" | diff.errors: 0
zones = []            -> validate: 1 error | gate.errors: 0, shape "e{}" | diff.errors: 0
zones = null          -> validate: 1 error | gate.errors: 0, shape "e{}" | diff.errors: 0
zones = 42            -> validate: 1 error | gate.errors: 0, shape "e{}" | diff.errors: 0
```

`Document.validate()` rejects all four at `src/dashboard/dock/model/Document.mjs:786` (`edge-zone "<id>" zones must be a JSON object`). The shape gate accepts all four and emits a **success fingerprint**.

**The downstream result is worse than #18004's symptom.** #18004's malformed document produced all-empty categories with `errors: []` — indistinguishable from "these two documents are identical". Here the malformed root's entire subtree is *erased* rather than emptied, so the differ reports every item as a **remove**, still with `errors: []`. A consumer asserting "no unexpected topology change" does not get a false pass; it gets a false, confident, error-free report that the whole layout was torn down. Both are fail-open; this one also fabricates content.

## The Architectural Reality

Both openings are the same pattern, and #18004's fix moved one of them without changing the other. In the `edge-zone` branch of the walk:

```js
const zones = node.zones || {};                    // <- container: no record check
…
if (!Object.hasOwn(zones, zone)) { return '' }     // <- #18004's fix, correct at the descriptor layer
```

`Object.hasOwn` on a non-record returns `false` for every canonical key in `dockZoneEdgeKeys` (`top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`, `center`) — verified directly for a string, an array, `null` and a number. So every zone is classified as *legitimately absent*, the walk emits a clean `e{}`, and `errors` stays empty. The pre-#18004 form (`node.zones?.[zone]`) behaves identically here, which is why this is pre-existing on `dev` rather than introduced by PR #18005.

The generalizable shape: **a fail-closed walk fails open wherever it reads a subtree through an optional chain or a `|| {}` default.** Every *node-type* read in this walk already has an error arm (missing node, cycle, unsupported type). Every *container* read does not.

`TopologyDiff` never calls `validate()` — it consumes `Document.computeShapeFingerprint(document || {})` and reads only `gate.errors` (`TopologyDiff.mjs:110`). So the gate is the sole door, exactly as #18004 established for the descriptor case, and the same provenance bound applies: documents arriving via `createSavedLayout` / `restoreSavedLayout` have already passed `validate`; the exposure is hand-authored fixtures, foreign or older-schema payloads, and Neural Link callers passing a constructed document.

## The Fix

Give the container read the same error arm every node-type read already has, before the per-zone loop:

```js
case 'edge-zone': {
    if (!Document.isJsonRecord(node.zones)) {
        errors.push(`fingerprint walk found a non-record zones container for edge-zone "${nodeId}"`);
        return '?'
    }
    …
```

`'?'` matches what the other error arms in this walk already return, and `errors.length` is what drives the `{fingerprint: null}` return, so no separate polarity plumbing is needed.

Open design question, same one #18004 left: whether the message should align word-for-word with `validate()`'s `zones must be a JSON object` so the two gates read as one contract, or stay in the walk's own diagnostic voice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Document.computeShapeFingerprint()` returns a non-empty `errors` array and a `null` fingerprint for an `edge-zone` whose `zones` is present but not a JSON record — covering at minimum a bare string, an array, `null`, and a number.
- [ ] An `edge-zone` with a well-formed empty `zones` record (`{}`) still fingerprints clean as `e{}` with `errors: []`. This is the legitimate case and the line must not be drawn on truthiness.
- [ ] `TopologyDiff.diffDockDocuments()` surfaces the error through its existing `${side} document failed the shape gate:` prefix for both the `before` and the `after` position.
- [ ] An arm pins the property that failed here rather than a per-specimen assertion: for each malformed container form, `Document.validate()` non-empty ⟺ `computeShapeFingerprint().errors` non-empty. #18004's arm asserts this per specimen, which is why the container drift was invisible to it.
- [ ] The arm asserts the categories too, not only `errors` — the current fail-open reports fabricated `removes`, so an arm checking only "the gate complained" would miss the more dangerous half.
- [ ] Mutation-checked: reverting the fix reds at least one arm, and the revert is stated. An arm that passes against the unfixed source does not count.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` stays green — in particular no existing fixture that currently fingerprints clean starts erroring.

## Out of Scope

- **Re-opening #18004 or PR #18005.** The descriptor fix is correct, in-scope for its ticket, and this is a different input class. Nothing here asks for that diff to change.
- **Changing `Document.validate()`.** As in #18004, it already behaves correctly; the gate is what disagrees with it.
- **Unifying `validate` and `computeShapeFingerprint` into one traversal.** Still the right eventual answer, still a contract-level refactor with blast radius across persistence and the render boundary. Two tickets have now deferred it; if a third arrives, that is the signal to stop deferring and scope it properly.
- **Auditing every container read across the dock model for the same pattern.** This ticket closes the one demonstrated instance in this walk. A pattern census is separate work and should be justified by more than two data points.
- **`prune()`'s behaviour on a non-record `zones`** (`Document.mjs:892` iterates `Object.entries(node.zones || {})` and then `delete`s from it). Adjacent, plausibly also wrong, not reproduced here, and not on this gate's path.

## Avoided Traps

- **Folding this into PR #18005.** #18004's Out of Scope explicitly forbids exactly this creep, and its author correctly filed rather than fixed when the same situation arose in PR #18002. Same discipline applies to me.
- **Treating `zones: {}` as malformed.** An `edge-zone` with no occupied zones is legitimate and common — the same trap #18004 named for absent keys. A fix keying on truthiness rather than on `isJsonRecord` would red real fixtures and get reverted rather than corrected.
- **Asserting only `errors.length > 0`.** The distinguishing symptom here is the *fabricated removes*, which an errors-only arm cannot see.
- **Calling this an incomplete fix of #18004.** It is not: #18004's ACs enumerate descriptor forms, and the PR satisfies them. Framing it as a miss would misattribute a pre-existing `dev` defect to a correct patch.
- **Trusting a log grep as a coverage instrument.** Noted because it bit the sibling lane: Playwright's CI reporters print no path for passing files, so "the filename does not appear" is an instrument limit, not evidence of absence.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — restores the documented fail-closed behavior of an existing contract; no ADR authority is touched and no public signature changes.
